title: Global power lifting criterion for adequate moduli over an affine base
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal X$ a quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic stack over $k$, $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $f:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism. Algebraic stacks and quasi-coherent algebras have the meaning in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and affine spectra use [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose the induced homomorphism $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$ is an isomorphism. If, for every surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras and every $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal C)$, there exist $N>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$ with image $t^N$, then $f$ is an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. In particular its power-lifting property holds on every affine etale base change, for all quasi-coherent algebras on that base change. Neither $A$ nor $\mathcal X$ is assumed Noetherian.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 4.1.8 (3) implies (2), Remark 4.1.3, and Remark 5.1.2 (canonical adequate moduli space). Read online https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the affine criterion in [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] with $\mathcal Z=\mathcal X$, $C=A$ and the given morphism $f$. Its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are hypotheses of the item. The first condition of that criterion is exactly the assumed isomorphism $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$. For its second condition, take any surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ and any global section $b$ of $\mathcal B$; apply the hypothesis of the item with its $\mathcal B,\mathcal C,t$ renamed $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,b$. This supplies precisely the positive exponent and lifting section required by the criterion. Thus $f$ is an adequate moduli space. The criterion quantifies over all quasi-coherent algebras and has no Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Alper, arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 4.1.8(3) implies (2), Remark 4.1.3, Definition 5.1.1 and Remark 5.1.2; read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Unpack condition (2) of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] for this $f$. For each affine etale morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, that condition quantifies over every surjection of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal X_W$ and every global section of its target, and gives a lift of a positive power. This is exactly the stated base-change clause. In particular no descent of either algebra from $\mathcal X$ is required.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Lemma 4.1.8(3) and Proposition 4.2.1(3),(4), in the etale-chart formulation of def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space; read online.

proof_origin.place: Assembly using the existing affine criterion and the reviewed definition; source checked online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q106-5ade09b9d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. One commit. It changes only the item's proof fields and adds the report; the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, there are no new nodes and fixes/ is empty. Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 is not in literature/, so I read it online. Lemma 4.1.8 (3)⇔(2) holds for qcqs X with no Noetherian hypothesis. Remark 4.1.3 says X→Spec A is adequately affine iff X is. Definition 5.1.1 defines an adequate moduli space as adequately affine plus O_Y≅φ_*O_X. Prop 4.2.1(3),(4) give base change and descent. So the item is true. Step 1 applies the ⇐ half of the affine criterion in the existing same-unit node lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality (unsplit, empty proof_deps, so no cycle), with Z=X and C=A. Its hypotheses (field k, Spec A an algebraic space, f qcqs) are all present, and the condition matches exactly, including arbitrary qc algebras and N>0. Step 2 just unfolds condition (2) of def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space, which is the item's 'in particular' clause; elementary is correct. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Edge cases: empty X forces A=0 and is vacuous; the identity of Spec A works with N=1; non-Noetherian A is allowed. The only citer, lem-sfb-power-lifting-quotient-submersive step 3, uses exactly this conclusion. No repair note applies, the base item had no proof, there is no SGA source and no tool_uses are needed. Advisory: the item is a special case of the etale-locality node, made by a different group on the same day; the maintainer may later mark it merged. The future split of etale-locality must not cite this item, or it would create a cycle.
